correctness.rationale: The equilibrium sine flow takes two alternating values. A negative conductance on the weighted cycle gives a negative Hessian form: two negatives by two-edge cutting, one negative by path resistance with m−1 equal positive conductances, giving R>(1/c), and zero conductance recurs on m parity edges causing a non-simple zero. Conversely all-acute edges are strictly stable. The principal inverse sine and winding quantization prove unique q branches for K>K_q and exclusion of others. The 2-cell Fourier decomposition gives all 2m eigenvalues and small-edge expansions produce the square-root q=0 and linear |q|>0 coefficients. The standalone verify.py passed 630 branch checks and independent Jacobian/spectrum comparisons; finite evidence corroborates but does not replace proof.

originality.rationale: The same alternating detuning model and winding branch equations are explicitly treated by Tilles et al. (2011), including numerical transitions 0.764 and 5.236 for ten sites; these are credited. What is not present in their inspected full text is a necessary-and-sufficient complete all-size FULL-phase-space stable-state theorem or exact distinct q-dependent critical spectral-gap exponents. Their discussion states low-dimensional stability can differ from full-space stability. Generic Roy–Lahiri and Ochab–Góra methods do not imply the global exclusion of all complementary inverse-sine branches. Targeted mathematical-literature and published-result searches found no subsuming result, with residual risk from arXiv:1102.3890 and unpublished equivalent specializations.
residual_risks: Tilles et al. (2011) already contain the exact alternating-frequency branch equations, sample crossing values, and near-onset full-space computations; priority applies only to the new complete full-space stability exclusion and explicit gap laws.
Closely related arXiv:1102.3890 full text was not accessible; an uninspected theorem there or another source could imply more than its abstract.

A general result on signed Laplacians or ring phase locking may imply the present instability lemma when specialized, even without discussing alternating frequency explicitly; this was not demonstrated by inspected papers.

value.rationale: A complete analytic stable-state count for every ring size and coupling resolves the specific full-space stability ambiguity highlighted in the earlier alternating-frequency paper. The exact q-threshold staircase and full Bloch spectrum distinguish multistability birth from relaxation, with q=0 square-root and nonzero q linear slowing and computable constants. These are structural, nontrivial results for a standard ring model, not a small arbitrary numerical slice. No claims are made about nonlinear threshold or basin geometry.
